### Observed differences

- In the later window, A19 and A20 appear much later in the case (mean relative position about 0.37 before vs about 0.66 after), while A21 and A22 appear much earlier (about 0.66 vs about 0.38); A23 and A27 keep roughly their positions (about 0.40→0.43 and 0.60→0.63). A19 and A20 occur in only about half of the traces (about 53 in 100 before, 48–53 after), while A21, A22, A23 and A27 occur in all traces. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- The main successors swapped: A19's outgoing transitions went from about 97 in 100 leading to A23 to about 95 in 100 leading to A28, and A20's from about 95 in 100 to A23 to about 96 in 100 to A28; conversely, A21 now exits to A23 in about 50 in 100 transitions (previously to A28 in about 47 in 100) and A22 to A23 in about 44 in 100 (previously to A28 in about 50 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- A27 now leads mainly to A20 and A19 (about 51 and 46 in 100 outgoing transitions) where it previously led to A21 and A22 (about 49 and 46 in 100), and A38 now leads to A22 and A21 (about 44 and 42 in 100) where it previously led to A19 and A20 (about 45 and 40 in 100). [DIR005, DIR007]
- Pairwise order flipped almost completely: before, A19 and A20 preceded A21, A22, A23 and A27 in about 46–54 in 100 cases and hardly ever followed them (at most about 1 in 100); in the later window they follow them in about 47–53 in 100 cases and hardly ever precede them. A23 and A27, which preceded A21 and A22 in about 97–99 in 100 cases, now follow them in about 97–99 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- Adjacency moved with the order: in the later window A20 directly follows A27 and directly precedes A28 (distance 1 in about 97–98 in 100 of about 105 supporting observations each, versus 1–2 observations before), the A27→A28 distance shortened from about 3 to 2 steps, and the A38→A23 and A37→A23 distances lengthened from about 2 to 3 and about 3 to 4 steps. [LAG001, LAG004, LAG007, LAG013, LAG017]
- A36 is executed less often: it appears in about 13 in 100 later-window traces versus about 25 in 100 before (mean occurrences per trace 0.40 vs 0.18), and A37 sends about 23 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A36 versus about 43 in 100 before, while A37→A38 rises from about 56 to 70 in 100. [OCC001, DIR006]
- Several lag comparisons involving A36, A37 or A38 with A19–A23 rest on only 1–3 observations in one window and carry little weight individually. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG012, LAG015, LAG016]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the placement of two activity groups was exchanged. In the earlier window A19 and A20 ran in the first part of the case and were followed by A23, while A21 and A22 ran late, after A27, and exited to A28; in the later window A21 and A22 run early and are followed by A23, while A19 and A20 run late, after A27, and exit to A28, with A38 now feeding A21/A22 instead of A19/A20. In addition, A36 is executed in fewer cases and receives less routing from A37. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR007, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, LAG001, LAG004, OCC001, DIR006]

This is a hypothesis about order and placement, and the relational evidence shows the change directly: the order between A21/A22 and A23/A27 flips in about 97–99 in 100 traces while these activities co-occur in all traces, so the flip is near-universal rather than a rare variant surfacing in one window; successor shares move by roughly 45–95 percentage points on about 100–200 outgoing transitions per window; and the position and adjacency changes point in the same direction. With 43 qualifying items against roughly 0.67 expected for an unchanged process, the set of results is far beyond what random re-splits of the pooled data produce. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG004, LAG007, LAG013, LAG017, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

Limitations: each window is a finite sample of 200 traces, so secondary share changes — notably A36's fall from about 25 to 13 in 100 traces and the small shifts for A23 and A27 — could partly reflect sampling differences in how often existing variants appear; in principle, a shift in the prevalence of two pre-existing variants (one per order) could mimic the flip if the minority order stayed below about 2 in 100 traces in each window. Several lag comparisons rest on 1–3 observations, and many items describe the same movement of the two groups, so they are not independent confirmations; positions are event positions, not clock times. [OCC001, POS005, POS006, LAG002, LAG005, LAG008, LAG010, LAG012, LAG015, LAG016]

Now let's understand the behavioural story.

OCC001: A36 occurrences decreased: mean per trace 0.40 → 0.18, participation 25% → 13%, recurrence 8% → 2%. Support 50 before, 26 after. Empirical strength 0.995.
